key_insight: Clipped decentralized SGD can achieve order-optimal convergence under heavy-tailed noise while preserving linear speed-up across agents, unlike normalization-based methods.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical distributed optimization recipe for federated and networked learning systems operating under noisy, non-Gaussian gradients.
method: Apply gradient clipping at each local worker before decentralized averaging.
Analyze consensus error so network effects appear only as higher-order terms.
Prove high-probability and expected rates for smooth non-convex objectives with bounded p-th moment noise, p in (1,2].
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees, linear speed-up, and numerical experiments that validate the clipped DSGD theory.
watch_item: Choosing the clipping threshold is important: overly aggressive clipping may distort gradients and slow optimization despite the convergence guarantees.
paper_title: Decentralized SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise: Optimal Convergence Rates and the Role of Gradient Clipping
